newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagrebacka mark loan sets new Croatia benchmark.
newsitem.headline: Zagrebacka mark loan sets new Croatia benchmark.

text.p: Zagrebacka Banka set a new benchmark for Croatia on the international loan market with its three-year 400 million mark syndicated loan, arrangers and bank officials said on Monday.

"The benchmark is not only in terms of amount, and it is the largest loan by a Croatian borrower, but also in terms of price," Momi Mullan of Chase Manhattan, one of four arrangers, told a news conference.

The annual interest was set at 50 basis points over Libor which Mullen described as "very aggressive". It beat 87.5 points that the state-owned oil company INA is to pay for a $150 million loan raised in May.
The syndication, drawing in 53 banks, was also said to be the largest yet by any commercial bank in central and eastern Europe.
"It indicates how deeply Zagrebacka has managed to penetrate. It could easily have raised 600 million marks," said Dietmar Stuhrmann of Dresdner Bank.
Zagrebacka plans to refinance a previous one-year loan, totalling 130 million Swiss francs, and will use the rest for increasing lending for its clients, said its chief executive Franjo Lukovic.
He said the bank might also consider further interest rate cuts after getting good terms on the loan. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
